_note:
CANONICAL CLUB VISUAL IDENTITY. This file holds VISUAL metadata only — colours used to art-direct fixture graphics. Factual football metadata about opponents (ground, founded, nickname) stays in data/opponents.json, which is human-verified and must never be polluted with inferred design data. Two files, two kinds of truth.

HOW A PALETTE BECOMES REAL: colours start null. js/brand-palette.js can SUGGEST a palette by sampling the club crest, and a suggestion is only ever a starting point — it lands as verified:false. A human opens Studio > Brand Library, looks at it beside the crest, edits if needed and confirms. Confirming sets verified:true. Locking sets locked:true, after which nothing automatic may overwrite it, ever.

WHY THE CARE: these colours are published under the Rayners Lane badge on graphics naming another club. Getting a club’s colours wrong is the visual equivalent of misspelling their name. An unverified palette is therefore never used on its own — the engine falls back to a neutral Rayners Lane treatment until a human has said yes.

_fallback._why: Used when a club has no verified palette. Deliberately neutral: a wrong colour is worse than no colour, and a grey counter-light still gives the composition depth without claiming anything about the opponent.

_verificationRule: AUTO-PROMOTION RULE. A suggested palette may be promoted to verified ONLY when the crest sample is large (confidence >= 0.9) and the dominant colour is genuinely saturated (>= 0.45). Those two together mean the badge has one obvious colour and the sampler saw enough of it — Harefield red, Burnham navy, Reading City yellow. Everything else stays neutral and is flagged reviewNeeded, because a guessed colour published under our badge on a graphic naming another club is not a cosmetic mistake. Promotion sets locked:false so staff can still correct it; a human confirming in Brand Library should set locked:true.
